metadata.description: Spark is a lending protocol built on an Aave V3 fork (SparkLend) with an integrated savings layer that routes deposits through the Sky (formerly MakerDAO) DAI Savings Rate (DSR) via the Pot contract. Governance decisions execute through the Sky governance stack — DSPause enforces a 24-hour delay before DSPauseProxy forwards calls to SubProxy, which holds admin rights on every SparkLend contract. An Asset Liability Management (ALM) layer controlled by three separate multisigs lets the protocol rebalance capital via arbitrary external calls. Price data comes from a mix of Chainlink, Chronicle, RedStone, and protocol-specific exchange-rate oracles for liquid staking and restaking tokens. The protocol currently secures $3.35B across SparkLend markets and the savings module.

admins.name: DSPauseProxy (Sky Governance Executor)
admins.description: The execution endpoint of the Sky governance stack. DSPause plots a governance spell here after the 24-hour delay, and DSPauseProxy then delegatecalls it — effectively routing every governance action against Spark contracts. It is the root admin of SubProxy, SDAO, ESM, and StarGuard. Because every upgrade and parameter change in SparkLend ultimately resolves to this contract, it controls $3.35B in reachable capital and the $379.40M SPK token supply.

admins.name: ESM (Emergency Shutdown Module)
admins.description: Sky's Emergency Shutdown Module. When enough MKR/SKY is burned into the ESM to cross a configured threshold, it can call `exec` on SubProxy to trigger Sky governance. In Spark's permission graph it appears as an admin of SubProxy, but it is only activated during a system-wide Sky emergency shutdown.

admins.name: StarGuard (Sky Authority Registry)
admins.description: Sky's authority contract registered as admin of SubProxy via the `can` access-control pattern. It whitelists which addresses may call which functions on SubProxy, and is itself administered by DSPauseProxy.

mitigations.label: spell-delay
mitigations.description: Invocation via StarGuard (SubDAO governance) requires a spell to be plotted on StarGuard and executed within the maxDelay window (7 days). Each spell additionally enforces its own `isExecutable()` off-chain delay (commonly a timestamp gate) before StarGuard.exec can delegatecall through SubProxy.

admins.name: SubProxy (Sky Governance Relay)
admins.description: Owned by DSPauseProxy and registered as the admin, owner, or `PoolAdmin`/`EmergencyAdmin` role-holder on virtually every Spark contract. Through its 116 permissioned entry points it can add/drop reserves, change interest rate strategies, upgrade ATokens via PoolConfigurator, change the price oracle, reassign access-control roles, and move treasury funds in Collector. Controls $154.37M in directly held contracts and $3.35B in reachable capital — essentially the full protocol.

mitigations.label: bounded mint
mitigations.description: Unbacked mints are capped per reserve by the `unbackedMintCap` configuration (settable only by POOL_ADMIN via PoolConfigurator.setUnbackedMintCap). Total outstanding unbacked supply cannot exceed the cap: `require(unbacked <= unbackedMintCap * 10**decimals)`. A reserve with `unbackedMintCap == 0` disables unbacked minting entirely.

mitigations.label: rewards-only
mitigations.description: Impact is contained to the protocol's incentives system (wstETH reward emissions). User deposits, withdrawals, and the underlying aToken lending positions are unaffected — the lending-side handleAction hook on ATokens is pointed by POOL_ADMIN, not by EmissionManager. The reward distribution uses a PullRewardsTransferStrategy (0x11aAC1cA..) that pulls wstETH from the Rewards Vault (2/3 GnosisSafe 0x8076...) via transferFrom on each claim. Neither the RewardsController nor the TransferStrategy itself custodies reward tokens. The cap is wired to `EmissionManager.rewardsVaultWstETHBalance` (a live on-chain read of the Safe's wstETH balance), so it updates automatically as the vault is topped up or drained.

mitigations.label: per-user reward theft
mitigations.description: setClaimer authorizes a third party to call claimRewardsOnBehalf(user, to=arbitrary), redirecting the targeted user's unclaimed accrued rewards anywhere. Bounded per call to that user's unclaimed balance, and system-wide to the Vault's live wstETH balance. Deposits, aTokens, and other users' rewards cannot be reached without a separate setClaimer call per victim.

mitigations.label: orphan pipe
mitigations.description: Only rewires the EmissionManager's internal pointer to a RewardsController. The ATokens keep their existing IncentivesController (set via POOL_ADMIN on each AToken), so existing accrual continues to be tracked on the old controller and remains fully claimable. Future emission configuration changes via EmissionManager will simply not reach the ATokens — a misconfiguration, not a fund-impact event.

mitigations.label: bounded retroactive
mitigations.description: configureAssets re-checkpoints the distribution using a caller-supplied `totalSupply` (not read on-chain), so a malicious emissionAdmin can retroactively skew accruals for the interval since the last checkpoint. Effect is bounded to emissionPerSecond × time-delta, and ultimately to the Vault's wstETH balance (tracked as EmissionManager.rewardsVaultWstETHBalance). setEmissionPerSecond reads scaledTotalSupply() on-chain and is not exploitable this way.

mitigations.label: claim-DoS
mitigations.description: Replacing the TransferStrategy does not transfer the old strategy's transferFrom allowance, so a malicious replacement cannot pull the Vault's wstETH unless the Safe signs a fresh approve. Worst-case is DoS on future claims (replacement strategy reverts or has zero allowance); already-accrued amounts persist and become claimable once the pipe is restored. Bounded by the Vault's live wstETH balance if a new allowance is granted.

It is a relay — the real authority is the owner multisig.

The cap is wired to `EmissionManager.rewardsVaultWstETHBalance` (a live on-chain read of the Safe's wstETH balance), so it updates automatically as the vault is topped up or drained.

mitigations.label: bounded retroactive
mitigations.description: configureAssets re-checkpoints the distribution using a caller-supplied `totalSupply` (not read on-chain), so a malicious emissionAdmin can retroactively skew accruals for the interval since the last checkpoint. Effect is bounded to emissionPerSecond × time-delta, and ultimately to the Vault's wstETH balance (tracked as EmissionManager.rewardsVaultWstETHBalance). setEmissionPerSecond reads scaledTotalSupply() on-chain and is not exploitable this way.

mitigations.label: rewards-only
mitigations.description: Impact is contained to the protocol's incentives system (wstETH reward emissions). User deposits, withdrawals, and the underlying aToken lending positions are unaffected — the lending-side handleAction hook on ATokens is pointed by POOL_ADMIN, not by EmissionManager. The reward distribution uses a PullRewardsTransferStrategy (0x11aAC1cA..) that pulls wstETH from the Rewards Vault (2/3 GnosisSafe 0x8076...) via transferFrom on each claim. Neither the RewardsController nor the TransferStrategy itself custodies reward tokens. mitigations.label: claim-DoS

Worst-case is DoS on future claims (replacement strategy reverts or has zero allowance); already-accrued amounts persist and become claimable once the pipe is restored. Bounded by the Vault's live wstETH balance if a new allowance is granted.

admins.name: ALMProxyFreezable
admins.description: The ALM execution proxy. It can call CapAutomator's `execSupply`/`execBorrow`/`exec` entry points, and serves as the contract through which the three ALM multisigs execute arbitrary calls. Protocol-internal — the real authority belongs to its controller multisigs.

admins.name: SparkLend Freezer 3/5 Multisig
admins.description: A 3-of-5 GnosisSafe that owns SparkLendFreezerMom and can instantly freeze or pause any SparkLend market without waiting for the 24-hour governance delay. Through SparkLendFreezerMom it calls `setReserveFreeze`, `setReservePause`, `freezeAllMarkets`, and `pauseAllMarkets`, blocking new borrows/supplies on all 22 reachable contracts (covering $3.35B in reachable capital). It cannot drain funds, only halt market activity.

admins.name: PoolConfigurator (AToken Upgrader)
admins.description: The upgradeable SparkLend configurator contract, itself administered by SubProxy. Internally it is registered as the admin on all 18 AToken proxies, meaning it can upgrade the AToken implementation backing any reserve — giving it direct control of $3.35B in AToken capital. A protocol-internal access-control relay, not a human-controlled admin.

admins.name: Pool (AToken Mint/Burn)
admins.description: The upgradeable SparkLend Pool contract. Its implementation is set by PoolAddressesProvider, so it is governed by SubProxy via upgrade. Internally it is the only contract allowed to `mint`/`burn`/`transferUnderlyingTo` on ATokens — the standard Aave V3 architecture. Direct capital: $154.37M.

admins.name: ALM Controller 1/2 Multisig
admins.description: A 1-of-2 Safe registered as a controller on ALMProxyFreezable, giving it `doCall`, `doCallWithValue`, and `doDelegateCall` — the ability to execute arbitrary calls and delegatecalls from the ALM proxy. The ALM proxy is a controller on 23 downstream contracts reaching $3.35B in capital; the 1-of-2 threshold means a single signer can trigger these calls.

admins.name: ALM Controller 2/5 Multisig
admins.description: A 2-of-5 Safe registered as a second controller on ALMProxyFreezable with the same arbitrary-call powers as the 1/2 Safe — `doCall`, `doCallWithValue`, `doDelegateCall` — reaching $3.35B in downstream capital. Two signers out of five are sufficient.

admins.name: ALM Controller Manager 1/4 Multisig
admins.description: A 1-of-4 Safe that can call `removeController` on ALMProxyFreezable, removing the other ALM multisigs from the controller set. A single signer is sufficient to execute this action, affecting $3.35B in reachable capital.

admins.name: Sky Governance Chief (DSPause Owner)
admins.description: The on-chain voting contract that owns DSPause and is authorised to plot and drop governance spells. Control is held by MKR/SKY token voters through the Sky governance system; any address with sufficient delegated votes can propose actions, which then execute after the 24-hour DSPause delay. From Spark's perspective this is the ultimate source of governance authority.

mitigations.description: Every authority-gated action is subject to the 1-day timelock: plot() requires eta >= block.timestamp + delay, and plan execution is deferred until eta.

admins.name: DSPause (Sky Governance Timelock)
admins.description: Immutable contract enforcing a hardcoded 86,400-second (24-hour) delay on every governance action before it can execute. Spells are plotted by the DSPause owner (the Sky/MKR voting Chief), wait 24 hours, and are then fired through DSPauseProxy. The delay itself can be changed only by executing a spell through DSPause.

mitigations.description: DSPauseProxy.exec is only callable by DSPause. Every invocation has already passed DSPause's 1-day timelock (plot → eta >= block.timestamp + delay → exec).
